requirements.quote:
To allow for better compression efficiency, the Cookie header field
   MAY be split into separate header fields, each with one or more
   cookie-pairs.  If there are multiple Cookie header fields after
   decompression, these MUST be concatenated into a single octet string
   using the two-octet delimiter of 0x3b, 0x20 (the ASCII string "; ")
   before being passed into a non-HTTP/2 context, such as an HTTP/1.1
   connection, or a generic HTTP server application.
requirements.condition: When representing a Cookie header field in HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: The Cookie header field may be split into separate header fields, each containing one or more cookie-pairs.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated HTTP/2 Cookie field lines can be inspected to verify that every split field contains at least one cookie-pair.

requirements.quote:
To allow for better compression efficiency, the Cookie header field
   MAY be split into separate header fields, each with one or more
   cookie-pairs.  If there are multiple Cookie header fields after
   decompression, these MUST be concatenated into a single octet string
   using the two-octet delimiter of 0x3b, 0x20 (the ASCII string "; ")
   before being passed into a non-HTTP/2 context, such as an HTTP/1.1
   connection, or a generic HTTP server application.
requirements.condition: If multiple Cookie header fields exist after decompression and are about to be passed into a non-HTTP/2 context.
requirements.required_behavior: Concatenate the fields into one octet string using exactly the two-octet delimiter 0x3b, 0x20 (ASCII "; ").
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not pass the decompressed multiple Cookie fields into the non-HTTP/2 context without first performing the required concatenation.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can decompress multiple Cookie fields, cross the non-HTTP/2 boundary, and compare the resulting octets and delimiter exactly.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 uses special pseudo-header fields beginning with a ':'
   character (ASCII 0x3a) to convey message control data (see
   Section 6.2 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: When a field is used as an HTTP/2 pseudo-header field to convey message control data.
requirements.required_behavior: Its name begins with the ':' character, ASCII 0x3a.
requirements.why_checkable: An encoded or decoded pseudo-header field name can be checked for the fixed initial octet.

requirements.quote:
Pseudo-header fields are not HTTP header fields.  Endpoints MUST NOT
   generate pseudo-header fields other than those defined in this
   document.  Note that an extension could negotiate the use of
   additional pseudo-header fields; see Section 5.5.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint generates pseudo-header fields and no extension has negotiated additional pseudo-header fields.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not generate pseudo-header fields other than those defined by this document.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated field blocks can be inspected for pseudo-header names outside the document-defined set.

requirements.quote:
Pseudo-header fields are only valid in the context in which they are
   defined.  Pseudo-header fields defined for requests MUST NOT appear
   in responses; pseudo-header fields defined for responses MUST NOT
   appear in requests.  Pseudo-header fields MUST NOT appear in a
   trailer section.  Endpoints MUST treat a request or response that
   contains undefined or invalid pseudo-header fields as malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When constructing or validating a response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Request-defined pseudo-header fields must not appear in the response.
requirements.error_behavior: An endpoint receiving a response containing such an invalid pseudo-header field must treat it as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A response containing a request-only pseudo-header can be injected and the endpoint's malformed-message handling observed.

requirements.quote:
Pseudo-header fields are only valid in the context in which they are
   defined.  Pseudo-header fields defined for requests MUST NOT appear
   in responses; pseudo-header fields defined for responses MUST NOT
   appear in requests.  Pseudo-header fields MUST NOT appear in a
   trailer section.  Endpoints MUST treat a request or response that
   contains undefined or invalid pseudo-header fields as malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When constructing or validating a request.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Response-defined pseudo-header fields must not appear in the request.
requirements.error_behavior: An endpoint receiving a request containing such an invalid pseudo-header field must treat it as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A request containing a response-only pseudo-header can be injected and the endpoint's malformed-message handling observed.

requirements.quote:
Pseudo-header fields are only valid in the context in which they are
   defined.  Pseudo-header fields defined for requests MUST NOT appear
   in responses; pseudo-header fields defined for responses MUST NOT
   appear in requests.  Pseudo-header fields MUST NOT appear in a
   trailer section.  Endpoints MUST treat a request or response that
   contains undefined or invalid pseudo-header fields as malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When constructing or validating a trailer section.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Pseudo-header fields must not appear in the trailer section.
requirements.error_behavior: An endpoint receiving a request or response with a pseudo-header field in its trailer section must treat it as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A trailer containing a pseudo-header field can be supplied and rejection as malformed can be observed.

requirements.quote:
Pseudo-header fields are only valid in the context in which they are
   defined.  Pseudo-header fields defined for requests MUST NOT appear
   in responses; pseudo-header fields defined for responses MUST NOT
   appear in requests.  Pseudo-header fields MUST NOT appear in a
   trailer section.  Endpoints MUST treat a request or response that
   contains undefined or invalid pseudo-header fields as malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a request or response containing an undefined pseudo-header field.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the request or response as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: An undefined pseudo-header can be injected and the endpoint's malformed-message handling observed.

requirements.quote:
All pseudo-header fields MUST appear in a field block before all
   regular field lines.  Any request or response that contains a pseudo-
   header field that appears in a field block after a regular field line
   MUST be treated as malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating a request or response field block containing pseudo-header fields and regular field lines.
requirements.required_behavior: Place every pseudo-header field before every regular field line.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A pseudo-header field must not appear after a regular field line.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat a request or response containing a pseudo-header field after a regular field line as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Field ordering is directly observable, and a deliberately misordered field block can test malformed-message handling.

requirements.quote:
The same pseudo-header field name MUST NOT appear more than once in a
   field block.  A field block for an HTTP request or response that
   contains a repeated pseudo-header field name MUST be treated as
   malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating an HTTP request or response field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The same pseudo-header field name must not appear more than once in the field block.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat a request or response field block containing a repeated pseudo-header field name as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Duplicate pseudo-header names can be detected in a decoded block, and receiver handling can be tested with such a block.

requirements.quote:
*  The ":method" pseudo-header field includes the HTTP method
      (Section 9 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 request contains the ":method" pseudo-header field.
requirements.required_behavior: The field carries the HTTP method.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded ":method" value can be compared with the request's intended HTTP method.

requirements.quote:
*  The ":scheme" pseudo-header field includes the scheme portion of
      the request target.  The scheme is taken from the target URI
      (Section 3.1 of [RFC3986]) when generating a request directly, or
      from the scheme of a translated request (for example, see
      Section 3.3 of [HTTP/1.1]).  Scheme is omitted for CONNECT
      requests (Section 8.5).
requirements.condition: When generating an HTTP/2 request directly and including ":scheme".
requirements.required_behavior: Set ":scheme" from the scheme of the target URI.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted ":scheme" value can be compared with the target URI's scheme.

requirements.quote:
*  The ":scheme" pseudo-header field includes the scheme portion of
      the request target.  The scheme is taken from the target URI
      (Section 3.1 of [RFC3986]) when generating a request directly, or
      from the scheme of a translated request (for example, see
      Section 3.3 of [HTTP/1.1]).  Scheme is omitted for CONNECT
      requests (Section 8.5).
requirements.condition: When generating an HTTP/2 request by translating another request and including ":scheme".
requirements.required_behavior: Set ":scheme" from the scheme of the translated request.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted ":scheme" value can be compared with the source translated request's scheme.

requirements.quote:
*  The ":scheme" pseudo-header field includes the scheme portion of
      the request target.  The scheme is taken from the target URI
      (Section 3.1 of [RFC3986]) when generating a request directly, or
      from the scheme of a translated request (for example, see
      Section 3.3 of [HTTP/1.1]).  Scheme is omitted for CONNECT
      requests (Section 8.5).
requirements.condition: When generating a CONNECT request.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include ":scheme" in a CONNECT request.
requirements.why_checkable: A generated CONNECT request's field block can be inspected for absence of ":scheme".

requirements.quote:
*  The ":authority" pseudo-header field conveys the authority portion
      (Section 3.2 of [RFC3986]) of the target URI (Section 7.1 of
      [HTTP]).  The recipient of an HTTP/2 request MUST NOT use the Host
      header field to determine the target URI if ":authority" is
      present.
requirements.condition: When an HTTP/2 request contains the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
requirements.required_behavior: Use ":authority", rather than the Host header field, as the authority information for determining the target URI.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the Host header field to determine the target URI.
requirements.why_checkable: A request with conflicting ":authority" and Host values can reveal which value the recipient uses for routing or target construction.

requirements.quote:
Clients that generate HTTP/2 requests directly MUST use the
      ":authority" pseudo-header field to convey authority information,
      unless there is no authority information to convey (in which case
      it MUST NOT generate ":authority").
requirements.condition: When a client directly generates an HTTP/2 request and has authority information to convey.
requirements.required_behavior: Generate ":authority" and use it to convey the authority information.
requirements.why_checkable: The generated request can be inspected for ":authority" and its conveyed authority value.

requirements.quote:
Clients that generate HTTP/2 requests directly MUST use the
      ":authority" pseudo-header field to convey authority information,
      unless there is no authority information to convey (in which case
      it MUST NOT generate ":authority").
requirements.condition: When a client directly generates an HTTP/2 request with no authority information to convey.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not generate the ":authority" pseudo-header field.
requirements.why_checkable: The generated request can be inspected to confirm that ":authority" is absent.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST NOT generate a request with a Host header field that
      differs from the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  A server
      SHOULD treat a request as malformed if it contains a Host header
      field that identifies an entity that differs from the entity in
      the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  The values of fields need
      to be normalized to compare them (see Section 6.2 of [RFC3986]).
      An origin server can apply any normalization method, whereas other
      servers MUST perform scheme-based normalization (see Section 6.2.3
      of [RFC3986]) of the two fields.
requirements.condition: When a client generates a request containing both a Host header field and an ":authority" pseudo-header field, after the values are normalized for comparison.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not generate the request if Host identifies an entity different from the entity identified by ":authority".
requirements.why_checkable: Client output can be inspected for normalized Host and ":authority" disagreement.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST NOT generate a request with a Host header field that
      differs from the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  A server
      SHOULD treat a request as malformed if it contains a Host header
      field that identifies an entity that differs from the entity in
      the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  The values of fields need
      to be normalized to compare them (see Section 6.2 of [RFC3986]).
      An origin server can apply any normalization method, whereas other
      servers MUST perform scheme-based normalization (see Section 6.2.3
      of [RFC3986]) of the two fields.
requirements.condition: When a server receives a request whose Host field and ":authority" field identify different entities after normalization.
requirements.error_behavior: The server should treat the request as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: A request with normalized Host/authority disagreement can be supplied and the server's malformed-message handling observed.

requirements.quote:
Clients MUST NOT generate a request with a Host header field that
      differs from the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  A server
      SHOULD treat a request as malformed if it contains a Host header
      field that identifies an entity that differs from the entity in
      the ":authority" pseudo-header field.  The values of fields need
      to be normalized to compare them (see Section 6.2 of [RFC3986]).
      An origin server can apply any normalization method, whereas other
      servers MUST perform scheme-based normalization (see Section 6.2.3
      of [RFC3986]) of the two fields.
requirements.condition: When a non-origin server compares the Host and ":authority" fields.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform scheme-based normalization of both fields before comparing them.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests using syntactically different but scheme-equivalent authority values can determine whether scheme-based normalization is applied.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that forwards a request over HTTP/2 MUST construct
      an ":authority" pseudo-header field using the authority
      information from the control data of the original request, unless
      the original request's target URI does not contain authority
      information (in which case it MUST NOT generate ":authority").
      Note that the Host header field is not the sole source of this
      information; see Section 7.2 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: When an intermediary forwards a request over HTTP/2 and the original request's target URI contains authority information.
requirements.required_behavior: Construct ":authority" using the authority information from the original request's control data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not rely on the Host header field as the sole source of the authority information.
requirements.why_checkable: A forwarded request can be inspected to compare ":authority" against original control data, including cases where Host differs or is absent.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that forwards a request over HTTP/2 MUST construct
      an ":authority" pseudo-header field using the authority
      information from the control data of the original request, unless
      the original request's target URI does not contain authority
      information (in which case it MUST NOT generate ":authority").
      Note that the Host header field is not the sole source of this
      information; see Section 7.2 of [HTTP].
requirements.condition: When an intermediary forwards a request over HTTP/2 and the original request's target URI contains no authority information.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not generate an ":authority" pseudo-header field.
requirements.why_checkable: The forwarded request can be inspected to verify absence of ":authority".

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that needs to generate a Host header field (which
      might be necessary to construct an HTTP/1.1 request) MUST use the
      value from the ":authority" pseudo-header field as the value of
      the Host field, unless the intermediary also changes the request
      target.  This replaces any existing Host field to avoid potential
      vulnerabilities in HTTP routing.
requirements.condition: When an intermediary needs to generate a Host header field and does not also change the request target.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Host field to the value of the ":authority" pseudo-header field, replacing any existing Host field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not preserve or use a conflicting existing Host value.
requirements.why_checkable: The generated Host value can be compared exactly with ":authority", including input cases containing a conflicting existing Host field.

requirements.quote:
An intermediary that forwards a request over HTTP/2 MAY retain any
      Host header field.
requirements.condition: When an intermediary forwards a request over HTTP/2.
requirements.required_behavior: The intermediary may retain an existing Host header field.
requirements.why_checkable: Intermediary forwarding behavior can be observed to ensure retaining Host is supported as a permitted behavior.

requirements.quote:
":authority" MUST NOT include the deprecated userinfo subcomponent
      for "http" or "https" schemed URIs.
requirements.condition: When generating or validating ":authority" for an "http" or "https" schemed URI.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The ":authority" value must not include the deprecated userinfo subcomponent.
requirements.why_checkable: The ":authority" value can be parsed and checked for a userinfo subcomponent in requests using either specified scheme.
